blocks.text: Good morning Cynthia,

Further to the note below, the screening searches on the candidate marks are complete. We have ordered full searches on each candidate that showed no obvious conflict on the federal register, and we will start our review as soon as the reports come back. That keeps us where we planned to be at this stage.

A clean screening result is a first pass and nothing more. It tells us a mark has earned the cost of a full search, which looks well beyond the register to state filings, unregistered business use and domain names. It does not clear the mark for use.

To keep us on schedule, please confirm the description of goods and services we are searching against, and let us know whether {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} expects to sell under any of these marks outside the United States. A reply by the end of next week lets us begin reading the full reports the day they arrive. If it is easier to talk these through, we are glad to set up a short call.
Regards
Working Session: Trademark Clearance for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}

Minutes of a working session held by video conference to go through the full search reports on the candidate marks and to agree the order in which the written analysis will be prepared. Minutes taken by Mary Bradley and circulated to everyone listed below.
Attendees
Matters Discussed

Search reports. Ashley Williams reported that the full reports have come back for every candidate mark carried forward from screening, that her review of the federal and state registrations in those reports is finished, and that the review of common-law and domain-name results is under way. She explained that the registrations are the easier half of the work, because each one states the goods and services it covers, whereas unregistered use has to be pieced together from websites, trade listings and business filings that seldom show how long or how widely a mark has been used.

Early observations. Ashley Williams said that no candidate has so far shown a conflict that would plainly rule it out, but that some candidates share a dominant term with registrations for related goods, and those will need closer analysis before anyone offers a view on them. Mary Bradley added that the written analysis will give a qualified view on each mark with its reasoning stated, that it will be marked privileged, and that nothing said in the session should be taken as clearance of any mark.

Goods and services. Cynthia Hunter confirmed that the description used for the searches matches the products {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} intends to sell under whichever mark it chooses, and said that related product lines are being discussed inside the company but have not been decided. Kelly Snyder explained that a mark which is clear for the present description is not necessarily clear for a broader one, so each analysis will state the description it relies on, and any later expansion of the range should be searched before the mark is used on it.

Use outside the United States. Cynthia Hunter said that sales abroad are possible in time but form no part of the present plan. Mary Bradley noted that the searches cover the United States only, that clearance in other countries would be a separate piece of work with its own scope and fee, and that the firm will not begin any such work without written instruction from the client.

Unregistered users. Kelly Snyder recommended a use investigation wherever the common-law results suggest that a business is trading under a similar mark without a registration, since a search report alone cannot show whether that use is current or how far it reaches. Cynthia Hunter asked what an investigation would cost, and Mary Bradley said that each one would be quoted before it is ordered and would go ahead only with the client's written approval.

Order of work. Cynthia Hunter asked that the analysis of the company's preferred candidate be completed first, because that is the mark its leadership is leaning toward, and the firm agreed. The analyses of the remaining candidates will follow in the order the client ranks them.
Actions Agreed

rows: Finish the review of common-law and domain-name results for each candidate mark.
Draft the written analysis of the preferred candidate, then of the remaining candidates in the client's ranked order.
Identify each unregistered user that warrants a use investigation and obtain a quote for the client's approval.
Send a ranked list of the candidate marks, and confirm in writing whether any product line beyond the searched description should be covered.
Review each written analysis before it goes to the client, and confirm that the docket carries an entry for every open item in this table.

blocks.text: The next step is the analysis of the preferred candidate, which Ashley Williams will bring to Mary Bradley for review before it is released to Cynthia Hunter.
Status Report: Trademark Clearance
Privileged and Confidential. Prepared at the direction of counsel.
Prepared for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} by Ashley Williams, Patent Agent. Responsible partner: Mary Bradley, Managing Partner.
The Matter at Its Midpoint
The clearance work has reached its midpoint on schedule. The search phase is finished and the written analysis has begun. We are working within the agreed fee.
No mark has been cleared yet. A view on each candidate will come from Mary Bradley, in writing, once the analysis behind it has been reviewed. Nothing in this report should be read as that view.
Progress Since the Working Session
We have made steady progress since we met with your team. Each item below is complete as of this report.

items: Review of the full search reports for every candidate mark, covering federal and state registrations, common-law use and domain names.
A draft analysis of your preferred candidate, prepared by Ashley Williams with Kelly Snyder. It is now with Mary Bradley for review.
A short list of unregistered users that, in our judgment, warrant a use investigation. Kelly Snyder has obtained a quote for the investigator's work, and it has gone to your team for approval.
Your team's written confirmation of the goods and services description, and its ranking of the candidate marks.
Docket entries for every open item, including partner review of each analysis and follow-up on the investigation quote.

blocks.text: What the Searches Showed
The registrations gave us the clearer picture. Some candidates share a dominant term with registered marks for related goods. The analysis weighs each of those on its own facts.

The common-law results were harder to read. A website or trade listing rarely shows how long a mark has been in use, or across how wide an area. That gap is the reason we have recommended investigation rather than reaching a view from the report alone.
The domain-name results added little that the other searches had not already shown. Where a registered domain matched a candidate, we checked whether a business was actually trading from it.
Work Ahead
Our work for the coming period follows the ranking your team sent us. Each item has a named owner and a docket entry.

items: Final analysis of the preferred candidate, once partner review is complete. Ashley Williams.
Analyses of the remaining candidates, in your ranked order. Ashley Williams, with Kelly Snyder.
Use investigation of any unregistered user your team approves, followed by a revised assessment of the affected mark. Kelly Snyder.
A written view on each candidate mark, qualified and with its reasoning stated. Mary Bradley.

blocks.text: Each written view will follow the same plan. It will set out the goods and services description it relies on, the registrations and uses that bear on the mark, and the reasons for our assessment. Where the evidence is incomplete, the view will say so plainly.

If your team settles on a mark, whether and when to file an application is a separate decision. We will raise it with you once the analysis is final, because the time between clearance and filing carries its own risk, described below.
What Could Change the Picture
We list these points so that none of them arrives as a surprise. Each is on the docket and is checked whenever the matter is reviewed.

items: Later filings. Our searches show the register as it stood when they were run. A third party could file for a similar mark before you do, and the longer the gap before filing, the greater that exposure. If the gap grows, we will recommend an update search.
Unregistered use. A search report cannot show whether an unregistered use is current or how far it reaches. An investigation can move our assessment of a mark in either direction.
Product range. Each analysis relies on the goods and services description your team confirmed. A broader range would need its own search before the mark is used on it.
Timing of decisions. The schedule assumes a prompt answer on the investigation quote. Any delay there moves the final view on the affected mark by the same amount.

blocks.text: Fees

The engagement is being carried out for the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.fee}} set out in the engagement letter. Work to date is within that fee, and we expect the remaining work to stay within it.

Two kinds of cost sit outside it. An investigator's charges are quoted to your team before anything is ordered. Clearance in other countries would be a separate piece of work, and we would not begin it without your written instruction.

We will send the final analysis of the preferred candidate as soon as Mary Bradley has completed her review. Questions on this report may go to Ashley Williams or to Mary Bradley at any point before then.
